scenarioStory.history: Patient is enrolled in home hospice for metastatic pancreatic cancer. Daughter and primary caregiver reports the patient's abdominal pain has been escalating over the last two hours, rated 9/10, unrelieved by two doses of her prescribed breakthrough oxycodone. Patient is awake, oriented, and able to communicate her wishes; she states she wants relief from the pain and does not want to go without it out of fear of side effects.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 62-year-old hospice patient with metastatic pancreatic cancer, awake and oriented, reporting severe abdominal pain unrelieved by her prescribed breakthrough oxycodone. → Pain and life-threat assessment performed: Crew performs a focused abdominal assessment to rule out a life-threatening surgical cause, scores the patient's pain, obtains IV access, and confirms the patient's hospice status and capacity to direct her own care. → Hydromorphone given despite opioid tolerance: Crew administers weight-based hydromorphone with continuous capnography monitoring, recognizing that her chronic opioid tolerance and hospice comfort-focused goals of care mean the dose should not be withheld out of fear of respiratory depression. → Pain reassessed, repeat dose given if needed: Pain is reassessed five minutes after the initial dose; because it remains only partially controlled, a repeat weight-based hydromorphone dose is given within the protocol's cumulative maximum, and the patient is transported in a position of comfort with her daughter accompanying.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Severe breakthrough abdominal pain, hospice patient with metastatic pancreatic cancer

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 62-year-old hospice patient with metastatic pancreatic cancer, awake and oriented, reporting severe abdominal pain unrelieved by her prescribed breakthrough oxycodone.

scenarioEvents.name: Pain and life-threat assessment performed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew performs a focused abdominal assessment to rule out a life-threatening surgical cause, scores the patient's pain, obtains IV access, and confirms the patient's hospice status and capacity to direct her own care.
relatedChecklist: Assess pain using Numeric Rating Scale (NRS); document 9/10 baseline
Assess abdomen for life-threatening causes (rigidity, rebound, pulsatile mass, distension)
Establish IV access to allow analgesia administration
Confirm hospice enrollment and consult patient directly on treatment wishes

scenarioEvents.name: Hydromorphone given despite opioid tolerance
scenarioEvents.description: Crew administers weight-based hydromorphone with continuous capnography monitoring, recognizing that her chronic opioid tolerance and hospice comfort-focused goals of care mean the dose should not be withheld out of fear of respiratory depression.
relatedChecklist: Hydromorphone 1 mg IV (68 kg × 0.015 mg/kg = 1.02 mg; max initial 2 mg, max cumulative 4 mg)
Apply continuous waveform capnography as early monitor for opioid-induced hypoventilation
Administer full protocol-dosed analgesia; do not withhold for fear of respiratory depression

scenarioEvents.name: Pain reassessed, repeat dose given if needed
scenarioEvents.description: Pain is reassessed five minutes after the initial dose; because it remains only partially controlled, a repeat weight-based hydromorphone dose is given within the protocol's cumulative maximum, and the patient is transported in a position of comfort with her daughter accompanying.
relatedChecklist: Repeat hydromorphone 1 mg IV after 5 min (cumulative 2 mg; max cumulative 4 mg)
Reassess pain score and vitals; transport in position of comfort

scenarioEvents.name: Opioid withheld over resp depression concern
scenarioEvents.description: The crew hesitates to give hydromorphone, citing concern for respiratory depression, despite the patient's normal respiratory status, established chronic opioid tolerance, and clearly stated hospice comfort goals. Her pain escalates and she becomes increasingly distressed.
relatedChecklist: Recognize hospice guidance: do not withhold opioids for fear of respiratory depression

checklist.title: Assess pain using Numeric Rating Scale (NRS); document 9/10 baseline

Hydromorphone 1 mg IV (68 kg × 0.015 mg/kg = 1.02 mg; max initial 2 mg, max cumulative 4 mg)

Reassess pain score and vitals; transport in position of comfort
